summary: Uta Reinöhl is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and was appointed Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg in 2026.

Ute Hüsken studied Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies at the University of Göttingen under Heinz Bechert (~1989–1995). Her career includes posts at Göttingen, Heidelberg University, and as professor at the University of Oslo (2007–2017).

Ute Wallenböck specializes in Sinology and Tibetology, earning degrees at the University of Vienna and Sigmund Freud University Vienna. She has held posts at the University of Vienna, Palacký University Olomouc, Masaryk University, and the University of Bonn (2024).

Uto von Melzer was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Graz (1919–1923), where he studied under Johann Kirste, Rudolf Meringer, and Hans Reichelt.

Utz Podzeit was an Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as Universitätsdozent at Vienna from 1969 and completed a research stay at the University of Madras (1972–1974).
V. Kameswari is an Indologist who has served at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as a supervisor and guide (attested 2026).
V. M. Subramanya Sharma is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as an Assistant Professor at Osmania University from 2011 to 2022 and at the University of Delhi beginning in 2022.

Vinayaka P. Bhatta is an Indologist and linguist. At Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, he served as head of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and as Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).
V. R. Srinivasan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who pursued PhD studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

Indologist V. Raghavan studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at the University of Madras (Ph.D. 1934). He taught at Madras (1934–1968), founded and was secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, and advised the Adyar Library (~1969–1979).

V. W. Paranjpe was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He served as Superintendent of the Publication Department at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1927) and as Professor Emeritus at Deccan College.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading by 2017 and held a post there in 2018.

Vairamuthu Kanagaraj is an Indology scholar who earned an MA at SASTRA (2025) and pursued a PhD at IIT Hyderabad (2026). He held researcher posts at NIIMH, Jayadev Memorial Rashtrotthana Hospital, and IIT Hyderabad.

Valaiyattur Venkayya was an Indologist and epigraphist educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as acting Government Epigraphist of Madras (~1903–1908) and Acting Government Epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India (1905).

Valdo H. Viglielmo studied Japanology and philosophy at Harvard, Penn, and in Japan. He taught at Harvard, Princeton, and several Japanese universities before serving as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa from 1965 to 2002.

Valentin Parisot was a French scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Normale Supérieure. He served as Professor of Foreign Literature at the universities of Rennes (1842–1847), Grenoble Alpes (1847–1853), and Douai (1854).

Indologist Valentin Trapp studied at the University of Munich, Visva-Bharati University, and Banaras Hindu University. His teachers included Hanns Oertel, Lucian Scherman, Walther Wüst, Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, Kshitimohan Sen, and Gyula Germanus.

Valentina Stache-Rosen was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (1944–1954) and completed further studies at SOAS and Deccan College.

Valentine Ball was educated at Trinity College Dublin. He served with the Geological Survey of India (1864–1881), was Professor of Geology and Mineralogy at Trinity College Dublin (1881–1883), and directed the National Museum of Ireland (1883–1895).
Valentino Papesso was an Italian Indologist who studied at the University of Bologna from ~1907 to 1911. He later served as Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Bologna from ~1926 to 1944.
